headline: Montlake pedestrian bridge over SR 520 closed through Friday for concrete repairs
blurb: WSDOT closed the pedestrian bridge over SR 520 at Montlake at 7 a.m. Monday to replace concrete panels, with reopening scheduled by 5 p.m. Friday, Oct. 23. Walkers and cyclists are detoured to the 24th Avenue E overpass.

headline: Sprinklers knock down mattress fire at assisted living building at 16th and Howell
blurb: A Sunday night fire in an assisted living building at 16th Avenue and E Howell Street was put out by the building's sprinkler system after a large Seattle Fire Department response.

headline: Medicaid now pays for reentry services for people leaving King County jail
blurb: A state Medicaid reentry pilot lets participating jails, including King County's, bill Medicaid for pre-release case management, treatment scheduling and a 30-day medication supply. It covers eligible enrollees at more than 40 facilities statewide.

headline: Classified Cinema hosts free 'secret movie' night at the Egyptian Theatre Oct. 27
blurb: Classified Cinema will host a free secret-movie screening at the Egyptian Theatre on Oct. 27 while the parties work toward a long-term deal for the Pike Street cinema.

headline: Former Battles member Tyondai Braxton plays an all-ages show at the Vera Project Oct. 20
blurb: Tyondai Braxton, who left Battles in 2010, brings his new album 'Splayed Werks' to the Vera Project on Tuesday, Oct. 20, at 7 p.m.

headline: Trick Bag showcase brings Debt Rag and Miscomings to the Sunset Tavern Oct. 21
blurb: Local DJ and music critic Martin Douglas curates the 21+ showcase featuring Olympia experimental-rock trio Debt Rag and Miscomings on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

headline: Salt-N-Pepa headline MoPOP's Icons of Pop Culture Gala in the 250-capacity Sky Church
blurb: Salt-N-Pepa perform at MoPOP's 21+ gala on Thursday, Oct. 22; tickets are $250.

headline: Drag performer Monday Mourning presents 'Elvira: Mistress of the Dark' at Northwest Film Forum
blurb: The Mourning Sickness series screens the 1988 cult film on Saturday, Oct. 24, at 8 p.m., all ages.

headline: Japanese techno producer Ken Ishii DJs Substation with Depth's Cory Simpson Oct. 25
blurb: Ken Ishii plays the 21+ Fremont club on Sunday, Oct. 25, alongside Cory Simpson, who heads Seattle's Depth techno crew.

headline: Belltown tiki bar Navy Strength to close Oct. 31 after 10 years
blurb: Co-owners Chris and Anu Elford cited an expiring lease and industry fatigue; the bar runs its horror-themed 'Nightmare on Wall Street' pop-up through closing night. A public sale of glassware, equipment and decor is planned for November.

headline: MoPOP's 21+ Halloween party goes retro sci-fi with an alien-invasion theme Oct. 31
blurb: 'Fashionably Undead' runs 8 p.m. to midnight with DJ Deejay Hershe, emcee Clara Voyance, a $500 costume contest and a museum scavenger hunt. Tickets are $43, $39 for members.

headline: Ghoul Talk hosts a drag and burlesque Halloween show at the Sunset Tavern Oct. 29
blurb: Drag headliner Jack King Goff appears with live sets from Heather Edgley and Pink Steam; Ghoul Talk closes with femme-fronted My Chemical Romance covers.

headline: Man arrested after West Seattle home break-in, police say
blurb: Police say a 41-year-old man tried to enter one home on Fauntleroy Way SW, then kicked in the back door of a second, unoccupied home, where officers found him in a bed. He was booked for investigation of residential burglary and attempted residential burglary and held on $25,000 bail; charges have not yet been filed.

headline: Police seek driver who posed as rideshare driver outside Pioneer Square bar
blurb: A woman told Seattle police she got into a car outside a bar on 1st Avenue South on Oct. 10 and jumped out at a red light in Kent after realizing the driver was not her Uber. Police said city cameras in the area were not working and are asking for tips at (206) 233-5000.

headline: SPD chief accepts review finding department damaged LGBTQ+ trust at 2025 Cal Anderson rally
blurb: Interim Police Chief Andre Sayles accepted an Office of Inspector General review finding SPD did not grasp LGBTQ+ community concerns at the May 2025 rally and counterprotest, and said the department will expand LGBTQ+ liaison work. A lieutenant recorded making a profane remark before arrests received a written reprimand after OPA sustained a complaint.

headline: Seattle awards $4.6 million to cut emissions in affordable housing buildings
blurb: The Office of Sustainability and Environment is funding retrofits such as electric heat pumps at nine housing providers and community organizations, with Plymouth Housing receiving $2 million. The grants are paid for by the JumpStart payroll tax.

headline: French psych-rock band Slift plays a free all-ages KEXP session Oct. 19
blurb: The pre-taped live set in the KEXP Gathering Space is free and first come, first served, and will air on KEXP later.

headline: KEXP hosts Bloodworks Northwest blood drives Oct. 29 and 30
blurb: The 'Music's In Our Blood' drives run 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. both days at KEXP, with appointments booked online.

headline: KEXP sets 'Music Heals: Grief' broadcast day for Nov. 12
blurb: The all-day programming on 90.3 FM will feature listener stories about music, loss and remembrance; listeners can submit stories and song requests now.

headline: Barrio Bounce and Manwell's 'Werk It Out' fill Kremwerk's Oct. 24 weekend lineup
blurb: The Kremwerk, Timbre Room and Cherry complex lists Barrio Bounce, Werk It Out with Manwell and MINTWHISPER, and Impact! Barkwave for the night of Oct. 24.

headline: KEXP reviews 'TACKYY,' new album from Seattle-rooted jazz artist Bobbyy
blurb: KEXP's Oct. 19 new-music reviews include the Dynamite Hill release from Bobbyy, now LA-based, whose background includes Seattle jazz bands.

headline: Ballard Light Rail Now Stuck Till 2042: Sound Transit Faces Locals Tonight at Nordic Museum
blurb: Sound Transit and city officials hold a forum Monday 6-8 p.m. at the National Nordic Museum on the Ballard extension voters approved a decade ago, now not expected until 2042 amid a $34.5 billion budget gap. CEO Dow Constantine and Councilmember Dan Strauss are expected.

headline: 'Hack the Planet' 90s-only rave marks a two-year anniversary at Timbre Room Oct. 23
blurb: The crew behind the Trainspotting Rave throws a Hackers-themed, 90s-only all-nighter Oct. 23, 10 p.m.-2 a.m., with Riki Healing, only/hank, Slynky b2b Solanum and LSDFJ. 21+.

headline: 'Space Age' futuristic drag cabaret invades Timbre Room on Oct. 30
blurb: Hosts Indie Scent and Kitty Vixen lead a Halloween sci-fi drag show with Clara Voyance, Chance Hazard and Scary-Ann. Doors 7 p.m., show 8 p.m.; $15 advance, $20 at the door.

headline: KEXP throws a free Gorillaz Halloween day party before the Climate Pledge show
blurb: A free Oct. 31 party, 4:30-8 p.m., at the KEXP Gathering Space with a DJ Morgan set, ahead of Gorillaz, Deltron 3030 and Little Simz at Climate Pledge Arena that night.

headline: Thao plays a KEXP in-studio session open to the public Oct. 29
blurb: Thao performs live on KEXP at 11 a.m. Oct. 29 in the station's NW Rooms studio, with the session open to the public.

headline: Francis of Delirium go live on KEXP Oct. 26, public welcome
blurb: Francis of Delirium play a public in-studio session at KEXP at 11 a.m. Monday, Oct. 26.

headline: Club TNT 'Fright Night' brings heavy bass and fast beats to Kremwerk Oct. 22
blurb: Club TNT's Halloween-season dance night runs Thursday, Oct. 22, 10 p.m. to 2 a.m., with DJ Lena, Nylondaughter, Lily G and TNT. 21+, very limited capacity.

headline: Pandora's PlayPen goes 'Monster~Esque' with a drag, burlesque and striptease show
blurb: The drag variety show hits Kremwerk on Friday, Oct. 23, with the show starting at 7 p.m.

headline: Modest Mouse play a KEXP in-studio session open to the public Oct. 27
blurb: KEXP lists Modest Mouse LIVE on KEXP for Monday, Oct. 27, in its NW Rooms studio, open to the public; Francis of Delirium plays a public session the night before.

headline: Another Night of Gunfire Rattles the Central District, 911 Calls Pour In After 2 a.m.
blurb: Gunfire at several Central District locations set off 911 calls starting around 2:23 a.m. Sunday, according to East Precinct radio updates. No injuries were reported.

headline: Lounge Dispute Turns Bloody: Patron Slashed With Folding Knife, Attacker Flees
blurb: A dispute between two patrons outside an entertainment lounge on 17th Ave SW near SW 98th St late Oct. 16 ended with one cut on the forearm by a folding knife, according to the King County Sheriff's Office. The victim was taken to Harborview in stable condition; deputies recovered the knife and the suspect remains unidentified.

headline: Teen Boy Gunned Down on Downtown Tacoma's Commerce Street; No Suspects Yet
blurb: Tacoma police found a teenage boy with life-threatening gunshot wounds near 1100 Commerce St. after a 2:23 a.m. shots-fired call Sunday; he died at the scene. Police say no suspects have been identified or arrested and the death is being investigated as a homicide.

headline: Gunpoint Carjacking Near UPS: Two Students Robbed, Cops Hunt Stolen Mazda
blurb: Two suspects robbed two University of Puget Sound students at gunpoint around 12:40 a.m. Oct. 11 near North 14th, taking their wallets, phones and a 2016 Mazda CX-5 with California plates. Tacoma police and Crime Stoppers are asking for tips to find the car.

headline: Seattle City Council to vote Tuesday on RV permit program and overnight parking limits
blurb: The Vehicle Resident Assistance Program proposed by Councilmember Dan Strauss would put $5 million toward outreach and safe lots and give free permits to eligible vehicle residents. Without a permit, RVs would be limited to two hours of street parking and barred from parking overnight anywhere in the city.

headline: Shootout Near Garfield High Sends Bullet Into 7th-Floor Hallway on 23rd Ave
blurb: Friday-night gunfire near the Garfield Teen Life Center and Garfield High School led police to block off E Jefferson and 23rd Ave. A bullet was found in a seventh-floor apartment hallway; no injuries were reported.

headline: Charlie's Queer Books plans a Capitol Hill outpost with a cafe, wine bar and event loft
blurb: The Fremont queer bookstore is taking the two-story former Post Options space at 1122 E Pike St., roughly double its current size, with a wine bar, a coffee shop and a 50-seat event loft. The owners are aiming to open in time for the holidays, with the cafe coming later.

headline: Pre-Dawn Whidbey Fight Ends in Stabbing; Teen Airlifted, 18-Year-Old Arrested
blurb: Deputies say a 15-year-old was stabbed in the chest and back around 3:30 a.m. Saturday during a fight among several juveniles at a Freeland home and was airlifted to Harborview in stable condition. An 18-year-old was arrested at his Oak Harbor home and booked on suspicion of first-degree assault.

headline: Thousands March From Westlake to Seattle Center in 'No Kings' Protest
blurb: Thousands marched Saturday from Westlake Park to Seattle Center, where a voting fair was held near the International Fountain, as part of nationwide 'No Kings' protests against Trump administration policies. KIRO reported no incidents or arrests.

headline: 'Bruce Lee Way' signs go up on South King Street
blurb: South King Street between 6th and Maynard Avenues South now carries honorary Bruce Lee Way signs, sponsored by Councilmember Eddie Lin. A local Jun Fan Gung Fu academy ran a fundraiser to help pay for them.

venue: Día de Muertos Festival / Short Run Comix Festival
headline: Coming up: Seattle Center's free Día de Muertos festival (Oct. 31-Nov. 1) and the Short Run small-press comix fest (Nov. 7).
blurb: Día de Muertos is at the Armory Food & Event Hall and is free; it includes altars, sugar skull workshops, performances and art. It began in South Park in 1998.

headline: Flatstick Pub tees off in Woodinville's 1909 schoolhouse
blurb: Flatstick Pub held its grand opening Oct. 17 in the restored Old Woodinville School, its largest location, with a links-style mini golf course across the second floor, Duffleboard, darts and 30-plus taps of Washington craft beer.

headline: 'Dangerous' CO2 Levels Empty Ballard Ave Businesses on Saturday Morning
blurb: Businesses on the 5400 block of Ballard Ave NW were evacuated Saturday while a Seattle Fire hazmat team found dangerous carbon dioxide levels and ventilated a building. Crews declared the air safe and reopened it around 12:30 p.m.; no injuries were reported.

headline: Shotgun With Drum Mag Found After Chase Ends Through Guardrail; Driver Lunges at Deputy
blurb: Pierce County deputies say a speeding pickup driver fled, crashed through a guardrail near 40th Ave SW and 96th St SW and ran before lunging at a deputy. Investigators say they found a shotgun with a drum magazine and other guns; he faces eluding, DUI, assault and other charges.

headline: Canceled shows at the New Everett Theater leave ticket holders chasing refunds
blurb: A promoter's canceled run of shows, including Richard Marx, a Bee Gees tribute and Pearl Jam cover band Corduroy, has left fans waiting on money after he filed for Chapter 13 bankruptcy. The theater's owner says it can't refund tickets it didn't sell and is offering credit toward other shows instead.

headline: $2.3 Million Rampage: Man Arrested in After-Hours Bellevue Office Break-In and Arson
blurb: Police say a 40-year-old man got into an office building on 108th Ave NE overnight Sept. 27-28, vandalized it, stole from the business and tried several times to set fires, causing an estimated $2.3 million in damage. A patrol officer spotted him on Bellevue Way; he was booked on burglary, arson and malicious mischief, with bail set at $300,000.

headline: Dawn Fire Guts Edmonds Gyro Joint, Shutters Westgate Village Strip
blurb: Crews from South County Fire and Shoreline found heavy smoke and flames inside the empty Gyro Makers around 5:45 a.m. Saturday and knocked it down in under 10 minutes, but the restaurant was heavily damaged and neighboring businesses were closed. The cause is under investigation; the owners suspect an electrical problem in the roof.

headline: Pre-Dawn Gunfire in Burien Leaves One Man Dead, Another Wounded; No Arrests
blurb: Deputies found a man dead near SW 130th St and 2nd Ave SW around 3:40 a.m. Friday, and a second wounded man was found minutes later, the King County Sheriff's Office said. No one has been taken into custody.

headline: The Head and the Heart headline Benaroya Hall's free post-renovation open house
blurb: Benaroya Hall threw a free daylong open house Sunday, Oct. 18, marking its first major renovation since 1998, with a 4 p.m. set by The Head and the Heart, a DJ set, Chinese American Bear with a Symphony string quartet, and flash tattoos from Mama Bird Tattoo.

headline: Dark-Money Complaints Hit Ex-Councilmember Sara Nelson's 'Pass-Through' Group
blurb: A progressive PAC filed complaints with the state PDC and Seattle's ethics commission alleging Seafor, the nonprofit Nelson founded, is an unregistered political committee hiding donors behind a $30,000 spend backing District 5 candidate Julie Kang. The group has not publicly responded to the allegations.

headline: Chewing-Gum Sting That Cracked Two 1980s Everett Murders Lands on '48 Hours'
blurb: Everett police used a gum ruse in 2024 to collect DNA from Mitchell Gaff, who pleaded guilty this year to a 1980 and a 1984 murder and was sentenced in May to life in prison. The case was featured on the Oct. 17 season debut of CBS's '48 Hours.'

headline: Shoplifter Bolts Out Emergency Exit With Full Cart, Ends Up Hiding in Bushes
blurb: Kent police, already parked in the Canyon Ridge Plaza Target lot on another theft call, chased a 53-year-old woman who fled through an emergency exit with a cart and hid in bushes. Police say she took 21 items worth about $753.

headline: Cop Caught on Bodycam Vowing to 'Hurt People' at Cal Anderson Protest Gets a Written Reprimand
blurb: OPA found SPD Lt. Matthew Didier acted in an 'unprofessional, escalatory, and disrespectful' manner when he told officers they were past talking during the 2025 counterprotest against a far-right rally in Cal Anderson Park. Interim Chief Andre Sayles issued a written reprimand; OPA had recommended anything from an oral reprimand to a two-day suspension.

headline: Two Arrested in Parking-Lot Killing of Des Moines Youth Football Coach
blurb: Des Moines police say two people were arrested and booked with help from U.S. Marshals, DOC and Valley SWAT in the Sept. 20 killing of a 31-year-old youth football coach, who police say was chased into a lot off Marine View Drive S and shot after an argument. Names and charges have not been released.

headline: Renton's bagged Flock plate-reader cameras may come down for good Nov. 2
blurb: Renton's roughly two dozen Flock license-plate cameras have been switched off and wrapped in black plastic since a 4-3 council vote in May; the nearly $170,000 contract lapses Nov. 2 unless the council acts. Police want them back, while the ACLU and DeFlock Renton cite privacy and data-sharing concerns.

headline: Fast-rising Seattle hip-hop crew 4UST Collective played a live set for The Stranger's Noise Complaint series.
blurb: Led by MCs Webb Wavvy, D. Mikey and Tyler Soze, with producer Qreepz and a live band.

headline: Mudhoney started their first Australia/New Zealand tour in more than a decade on Oct. 16 in Melbourne. It runs through Nov. 1 in Auckland.
blurb: 14 dates, including Brisbane's Zed 51 Festival on Oct. 24.

headline: Hazmat Crews Swarm Rep. Jayapal's Seattle Office Over Suspicious Package
blurb: Hazmat crews checked a building in the 2000 block of 6th Avenue on Friday after U.S. Rep. Pramila Jayapal's Seattle office received a suspicious package; no injuries were reported and the area was cleared. Jayapal said it resembled mailings sent to members of Congress and election officials nationwide and called the effort an attack on democracy.

headline: Salon Revolt: 60+ Gene Juarez Stylists Stage 'Sick-Out' Over Pay Cuts
blurb: More than 60 Gene Juarez employees called in sick Friday, forcing appointment cancellations at salons across western Washington, in protest of a pay-scale change they say could cut pay up to 10%. The non-union workers want good-faith talks; the company said it respects its artists' right to be heard and leadership is meeting with staff.

headline: Pre-Dawn Gunfire in Burien Leaves One Man Dead, Another Wounded
blurb: King County deputies found a man dead at SW 130th Street and 2nd Avenue SW around 3:40 a.m. Friday, then were led to a second man with non-life-threatening gunshot wounds. No arrests had been made and Major Crimes detectives were interviewing witnesses.

headline: BOOTY.99 goes pink: TITTY.99 fundraiser night at Cherry
blurb: Cherry Nightclub's monthly BOOTY.99 party got a Breast Cancer Awareness Month makeover as TITTY.99, with DJs flotussin and Exis and part of the $10-$15 door going to Sisters Network Inc.

headline: Two Shot Overnight in Fairwood; Drone and K9 Can't Find the Gunman
blurb: Two people were shot late Thursday near SE 179th St and 114th Pl SE outside Renton and taken to Harborview and Valley Medical Center in stable condition. The King County Sheriff's Office has made no arrests and released no suspect description.

headline: White-Powder Letter Mailed to WA Elections Office Weeks Before Midterms
blurb: Law enforcement intercepted an envelope containing white powder addressed to the Washington secretary of state's elections division on Oct. 15. The U.S. Postal Inspection Service is investigating amid a nationwide wave of suspicious mailings to election and congressional offices.

headline: PIT Maneuver Ends Burien Chase: Stolen Car, Meth, Fentanyl and $5,600 in Fake Bills
blurb: King County deputies say a driver sped through Burien neighborhoods, fled onto Highway 509 and ran on foot after a PIT stop before being caught. The sheriff's office says the car was stolen and held crystal meth, powdered fentanyl, scales, a CO2 gun and $5,610 in counterfeit bills.

headline: Escapee From Unfenced Youth Home Gets 17.5 Years for 2022 Sex Assaults
blurb: A man who walked away from a low-security juvenile group home in Ephrata in 2022 was sentenced to about 17.5 years after pleading guilty to second-degree rape and indecent liberties for attacks at Southcenter Mall and in Seattle weeks later. King County prosecutors say they were never told about the escape; the state says the facility followed its protocol.

headline: Seattle social housing developer unveils first project, a 20-unit Central District building
blurb: The city's voter-created social housing developer plans a $15 million, mostly family-sized building next to the Central District library branch. It hopes to open by 2028.

headline: The Independent Pizzeria closes after nearly 17 years on East Madison
blurb: The Madison Park pizzeria served its final day Oct. 16 as its owners retire, two days earlier than planned so they could pack up. The space is passing to a new owner.

headline: Portage Bay Cafe's West Seattle Junction location serves its last brunch Oct. 25
blurb: The California Ave SW cafe is closing after nearly four years, citing limited indoor seating and rising costs; its other four Seattle locations stay open.

headline: Fremont holds its first-ever Zombie Crawl tonight (Oct 17), with drink deals for costumed zombies at 10 bars and a Thriller dance-off at Fremont Social.
blurb: Saturday, Oct. 17 in downtown Fremont; the Fremont Chamber shared the event on Instagram.

headline: The second Seattle Trans Underground Film Festival runs Oct. 15-18 at Northwest Film Forum. It fills the gap left when TRANSlations ended after 20 years.
blurb: Programmed by Sophie Amity Debs and Kory Caldwell. Last year's first festival sold out nearly every screening.

headline: FBI 'Most Wanted Fraudster' Dragged Back From India Over $600K Food-Stamp Scheme
blurb: A 64-year-old Kent man who owned a Tacoma grocery store was extradited from India to face six counts of wire fraud; prosecutors allege he ran SNAP cards for set amounts, handed back half in cash and pocketed the rest. Authorities say he fled to Canada and then India after his April indictment; he has pleaded not guilty.

headline: Arrest in Arson That Gutted Ex-NFL Star Desmond Trufant's Luxury Venue
blurb: Tacoma police arrested a man Wednesday in a fire officials say was intentionally set at The Sunset Estate, the event rental owned by former Husky and NFL cornerback Desmond Trufant; the house was a total loss. Trufant told police someone had turned on the gas at the property the day before the blaze.

headline: Homelessness Agency's Hidden Hole Hits $17 Million, Report Finds
blurb: A consultant's report found the King County Regional Homelessness Authority left Seattle and King County with at least $16.7 million in previously unreported costs, largely from administrative overspending, plus $4.4 million in interest owed to the county. Officials say repayment could take years, and the agency's board will decide on accountability Nov. 6.

headline: Cyclist Killed in Foggy Dawn Crash; I-90 Ramps Shut for Hours
blurb: A car struck and killed a bicyclist on northbound Bellevue Way SE near SE 30th Street around 6:30 a.m. Thursday in dark, foggy conditions; police said the driver was not suspected of impairment. Both I-90 off-ramps to Bellevue Way were closed until about 11:30 a.m.

headline: Fall City Teen Accused of Killing Parents and Siblings Will Face Adult Court
blurb: A King County juvenile judge ruled a 17-year-old accused of fatally shooting his parents and three younger siblings in 2024 will be tried as an adult on five counts of first-degree murder and one count of attempted murder. Prosecutors allege the killings were premeditated and that he called 911 and blamed a sibling.

headline: ICE Still Mining WA Driver Data: 356 Arrests Despite Sanctuary Laws, UW Finds
blurb: A UW Center for Human Rights study documents 356 arrests on Washington roads that followed federal agents querying Department of Licensing data, through pathways including the Nlets data-sharing network. Researchers say the state's efforts to restrict access have been ineffective and expect queries to rise.

headline: Judge Lets Boeing Door-Plug Victims Pursue Punitive Damages Fight
blurb: A King County Superior Court judge rejected Boeing's bid to block punitive damages in a suit by 47 plaintiffs over the 2024 Alaska Airlines Flight 1282 door-plug blowout. Plaintiffs argue Illinois law could apply to decisions made at Boeing's former Chicago HQ; trial is set for Feb. 1.

headline: Flash-Bangs and Chemical Munitions End Hours-Long Tukwila SWAT Standoff
blurb: Valley SWAT took a man into custody Tuesday night after he barricaded himself in an apartment in the 3700 block of Southcenter Boulevard, using distraction devices and then chemical munitions under a judge-signed warrant. Police say he faces first-degree burglary and felony harassment charges.

headline: Champagne bar Bong Bóng Bar lands at Harvest in Woodinville
blurb: The Infatuation just added Bong Bóng Bar, a Champagne-focused bar at Harvest at Woodinville pouring bubbles alongside Vietnamese small plates like fresh rolls and bánh mì boards, to its new-openings list.

venue: Rosette, Death & Co., The Ink Drinker, Majnoon and others
headline: Seattle magazine's fall drinking guide points to a zero-proof wave: Rainier Beach's Rosette specializes in no-alcohol cocktails, and Death & Co., The Ink Drinker and Majnoon all list NA drinks.
blurb: Rosette (Rainier Beach) opened in 2025 and specializes in zero-proof cocktails, plus natural and biodynamic wines.

headline: Gunman Buys an Item, Walks Behind Counter, Kills Belltown Gas Station Clerk
blurb: A clerk was shot and killed early Tuesday at a gas station near the Space Needle; police say a heavy-set man in black made a purchase, went behind the counter and fired, apparently taking nothing. No suspect was in custody.

headline: Fake-ID Thief Accused of Grabbing Costco Gold Bars From UPS Drivers
blurb: Snohomish County prosecutors charged a 21-year-old student-visa holder with identity theft and theft, accusing him of using fake licenses to intercept UPS deliveries of gold bars, silver coins and jewelry from Mill Creek to Issaquah. Investigators put the alleged haul at about $380,000.

headline: Inmate Bolts From Work Crew by Puyallup River, Caught in Auburn Hours Later
blurb: A state prisoner serving time for robbery and burglary escaped a work crew near the Puyallup River in Tacoma around 12:30 p.m. Tuesday. He was found in Auburn about 90 minutes later.

headline: Heavens to Betsy (Corin Tucker and Tracy Sawyer) bring their first album in more than 30 years to Neumos Nov. 5. Genesis Owusu moved up from Hidden Hall to Neumos because of demand.
blurb: Heavens to Betsy, the Olympia duo, released 'Baby's Gone,' which the article calls a '16-track mission statement.' The show is 21+ and $35.

headline: SPD Lieutenant Demands $3 Million, Alleging Racism and Retaliation
blurb: Seattle Police Lt. John O'Neil filed a $3 million tort claim alleging racial discrimination, harassment and retaliation, saying officers resist his leadership because he is Black. The city previously settled with four female officers who accused him and former brass of harassment; the city declined comment.

headline: 50 Shell Casings at Kerry Park: Two Shot at 3:30 a.m. Street Party, Juvenile Arrested
blurb: Two men were shot near Kerry Park early Saturday and police recovered about 50 rifle and handgun casings; officers stopped a car with a rifle inside and arrested a juvenile on assault charges. Both men were in serious but stable condition at Harborview.

headline: Drive-By Getaway SUV Runs Red Light, Slams Into Sheriff's Patrol Car
blurb: After a Friday-night drive-by on Meridian near 136th Street, a fleeing SUV ran a red light and disabled a Pierce County sergeant's patrol vehicle; two 22-year-old men were arrested at a Fred Meyer lot. Deputies say they found shell casings and an open tequila bottle, and a gun tossed from the SUV was stolen.

headline: 2 a.m. Bar Brawl Ends With Stolen Car Plowing Into Four Pedestrians
blurb: Police say a large fight broke out behind a North Everett restaurant early Sunday, and a man took a customer's car and struck several people while speeding away. Four pedestrians were hospitalized; the driver crashed a block away and escaped on foot.

venue: Nightclub on the 5800 block of 4th Ave S
headline: A drive-by shooting in a South Seattle nightclub parking lot killed a 36-year-old security guard and wounded a 27-year-old woman early Oct. 11; the getaway car was found burning.
blurb: Police responded just before 1 a.m. Sunday, Oct. 11, to the 5800 block of 4th Avenue South (SPD South Precinct). Hoodline calls it a Georgetown nightclub; KOMO describes it as a strip club.

headline: Nightclub Guard Killed in Drive-By; Getaway Car Found in Flames
blurb: A 36-year-old security guard was killed and a 27-year-old woman shot in the leg in a drive-by outside a south Seattle nightclub just before 1 a.m. Sunday. Police found the suspect vehicle burning less than an hour later; no arrests were reported.
